<a id="makerdubtiming"></a>

## `MakerDubTiming`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Api.Maker.Editor.MakerDubTiming` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

"A dub is never cut off" (DS-03 Must 7, 2026-11-07): the timing rules the adapter's dub hold (`MakerDubHold`) applies, pure so they are unit-tested.

**The hold.** When the game is about to move on from a line (`ScenarioReader.AutoNext`) while a clip that is not the game's own is still playing - a language set's take, a dub Pack Maker swapped in, a pack's global replacement, a mod's clip - it waits until that clip has played plus [`ReadingTime.VoiceTailSeconds`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Subtitles.md#readingtime--voicetailseconds). This is the same `clip + 0.3 s` part of the subtitle hold's rule (`max(2.5 s, characters / 15, clip + 0.3 s)`), applied in every language and to every row, voiced or wordless, because the next voiced row stops the voice and the end of a scenario closes the box. It matters where the game stops waiting for the voice by itself: the 30 s timeout of its `VoiceText` and `PomodoroVoiceText` rows.

**Stopped clips.** When the game already reports the voice finished (the clip ended, or a click or a skip stopped it), at most the 0.3 s tail is added, so a clip stopped early never freezes the box for the rest of its length.

**The game's own caps.** Two lines have a hard limit outside the scenario reader: the greeting at game start (20 s, then the story is ended) and the talk when a timer ends (15 s). While dubs can play those limits are multiplied by [`MakerDubTiming.MaxDubRatio`](#makerdubtiming--maxdubratio), the longest dub-to-original ratio seen in the wild; both scenarios still end by themselves first.

<a id="makereditrules"></a>

## `MakerEditRules`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Api.Maker.Editor.MakerEditRules` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The Pack Maker editor's input rules and the pack-relative paths it may write (ticket DS-03, CONTRACT.md "Principles" and "Segments").

The maker routes (DS-01) already refuse a malformed segment with 400 before the editor is called; the editor checks again here, because it is the one that turns the segments into file paths, and a second gate costs nothing.

Pack Maker writes exactly two kinds of file inside a pack, `data/subtitles/<lang>.json` and `audio/voice/<lang>/<clip>.wav`, plus its own bookkeeping under [`MakerEditRules.BackupFolder`](#makereditrules--backupfolder) (moved-aside creator files and the ledger of what it wrote). The loader never reads that folder: `PackContentIndex` gives it no meaning.

<a id="makerpackfiles"></a>

## `MakerPackFiles`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Api.Maker.Editor.MakerPackFiles` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Every file operation Pack Maker performs inside one pack folder: safe path resolution, atomic writes, moving creator files aside into [`MakerEditRules.BackupFolder`](#makereditrules--backupfolder) and back, and the ledger of the files Pack Maker itself wrote.

**Safe paths.** A path is taken relative to the pack root, normalised with [`PackContentIndex.Normalise`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.md#packcontentindex--normalise) (no `..`, no drive, no reserved device name), and must still lie under the root once made absolute. No folder between the root and the file may be a symbolic link or junction, so a link planted inside a pack cannot send a write elsewhere. (The root itself may be a link: a creator's working folder linked into `CWYLS Mods` is fine.)

**Atomic writes.** The bytes go to a hidden temporary file in the same folder (`.<name>.<random>.maker-tmp`: hidden, so a pack rescan in between never indexes it), are flushed to disk, then replace the target in one rename. A crash leaves either the old file or the new one, never half of either.

**Creator files are never deleted.** A file Pack Maker has to displace is moved to the same path under [`MakerEditRules.BackupFolder`](#makereditrules--backupfolder) (a dated name when that is taken, so no backup is ever overwritten). Pack Maker deletes only a file whose current bytes match what its ledger ([`MakerEditRules.LedgerPath`](#makereditrules--ledgerpath)) says it wrote there.

Not thread-safe on its own: the editor serialises its writes.

<a id="makersubtitlefile"></a>

## `MakerSubtitleFile`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Api.Maker.Editor.MakerSubtitleFile` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Sets or removes one entry of a flat JSON object - a pack's `data/subtitles/<lang>.json` - by editing the text, not by re-serialising it.

A translator's table is hand-written and diffed line by line, so the edit touches only the one member: every other key keeps its place, its spelling and its escapes, and the file keeps its indentation, its line endings and its trailing newline. A new key goes after the last one, written in the style the file already uses (the separator before the last member, the `": "` after its key, and `\uXXXX` escapes when the file holds no raw non-ASCII text). An empty or missing file gets two-space indentation.

A file that is not a strict JSON object ([`JsonReader`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Json.md#jsonreader): no comments, no trailing commas, no duplicate keys) is refused rather than "repaired": the creator's file is never rewritten from a guess. The result is parsed again before it is returned, so a bug here cannot write a broken table.

The BOM is the caller's business: pass the text without it and write it back as it was.

<a id="makersubtitlefile--apply"></a>

### `static MakerSubtitleEdit Apply(string existing, string id, string text)`

Sets (`text`) or removes (null) the entry `id`.

**Parameters**

- `existing`: The file's current text without a BOM; null or blank when there is no file.
- `id`: The key; required.
- `text`: The new value, or null to remove the key.

**Returns:** The new text, or why the edit is refused. Never null.

<a id="makersubtitlefile--read"></a>

### `static string Read(string json, string id)`

The text of one entry of a table, or null when it has none (or the table is not valid).

**Parameters**

- `json`: A table's text; null or blank means no table.
- `id`: The key.

<a id="makerwav"></a>

## `MakerWav`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Api.Maker.Editor.MakerWav` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Checks an uploaded dub before anything is written: a RIFF/WAVE file of 16-bit PCM, mono or stereo, 8-48 kHz, at most 60 s and 16 MiB (CONTRACT.md "Request rules" and "Routes"); and rewrites an accepted one as a canonical 44-byte-header PCM file.

Every refusal names what the file actually is - "24-bit PCM", "32-bit float", "WAVE\_FORMAT\_EXTENSIBLE, 24-bit", "an Ogg Vorbis file" - so the fix in the creator's audio editor is obvious. A WAVE\_FORMAT\_EXTENSIBLE file whose sub-format is 16-bit PCM is the same samples under a longer header (several editors write it), so it is accepted and normalised.

**Strict header (DS-10a).** Exactly one `fmt` and one `data` chunk, every chunk inside the size the RIFF header declares, byte rate = sample rate x block align, block align = channels x 2, and a `data` chunk of whole sample frames. Anything else is refused as `unsupported_media_type`: a file that two readers could read two ways never reaches the disk, and the length checked here is the length the game plays.

The canonical rewrite ([`MakerWav.Canonical`](#makerwav--canonical)) keeps the samples byte for byte and drops every other chunk (`LIST`, `bext`, cue points), so both the loader's own WAV parser and the engine's decoder read the saved file the same way.

<a id="makerwav--canonical"></a>

### `static byte[] Canonical(byte[] bytes, MakerWavReport check)`

The accepted dub as a canonical file: a 44-byte RIFF/fmt/data header and the samples, unchanged.

**Parameters**

- `bytes`: The uploaded bytes `check` was made from.
- `check`: An accepted check.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The check is not an accepted one.

<a id="makerwav--inspect"></a>

### `static MakerWavReport Inspect(byte[] bytes)`

Validates an uploaded dub. Never throws for bad input.

**Parameters**

- `bytes`: The request body.
